LESS SWITCHING. MORE WATCHING.

From subtitle to meaning.
Without losing your place.

01

Open your video

Play a local MKV or MP4, or paste a direct HTTP/HTTPS media stream. Use embedded text subtitles or bring your own subtitle file.

02

Click the unfamiliar bit

Select a subtitle word to see its Burmese meaning. Known phrases are matched automatically, so the expression stays together.

03

Take it in. Keep going.

Playback pauses on word click by default. Read at your pace, close the card and continue. You can turn automatic pause off in settings.

A FEW USEFUL DETAILS

Before you
press play.

The essentials, without the fine print.

Read the project documentation
Is it free? Do I need an account?

Yes. Subtitle Bridge is free and open source. Normal playback and offline dictionary lookup don’t require an account or a translation API key.

Does it work without the internet?

Local playback and English → Burmese dictionary lookup work offline once the required tools are installed. First installation downloads mpv and FFmpeg, so it needs internet access. Streams, update downloads and reports also need a connection.

Which subtitles can I click?

Supported text subtitles are SRT/SubRip, ASS and SSA, embedded or external. Image subtitles such as PGS and VobSub are not clickable text. The interactive overlay prioritizes readable dialogue and doesn’t recreate every ASS styling effect.

Can I paste a link from any video website?

The Stream URL field opens direct HTTP/HTTPS media streams, including Stremio’s localhost stream URLs. A normal webpage link usually isn’t a media stream. Subtitle Bridge doesn’t extract video from arbitrary websites.

Optional one-click Stremio handoff uses a reversible local compatibility patch. It isn’t an official Stremio integration.

What if a translation is missing or incorrect?

The dictionary is broad, but not exhaustive. Its AI-generated entries haven’t all received native-speaker editorial review. Use the report flag in the translation card to send the word or phrase for manual review.

Reporting is opt-in. It sends the term, report type and app/dictionary versions, without subtitle context, video paths or stream URLs. No report is sent just because you looked something up.

Does it support macOS or Linux?

The current stable download is for Windows x64 only. There is no stable macOS or Linux installer on this page.

Why might Windows show a publisher warning?

The current installer is unsigned, so Windows may show an Unknown Publisher or SmartScreen warning. Use the official GitHub download linked here; checksums are available on the release page.
